applicability: any two real numbers a, b: the identity a% of b = b% of a holds unconditionally because a% of b = (a·b)/100 and multiplication is commutative. Use the swap whenever the flipped form is easier to compute mentally — typically when one of the two numbers is small or round.

steps.working: a% of b = b% of a

draw.note: First draw is the percent (6), second is the amount (76). Range covers small single-digit percents up to two-digit values; presentation filter enforces 1-2 digit rendering only.

nulls.reason: The identity a% of b = b% of a follows from a% of b = (a·b)/100 and commutativity of multiplication in the reals; there is no numeric case where the simple rule fails. Verifier is asked to confirm exhaustively over integers a, b in [0, 100].
